title: The parity conjecture for Game of Cycles gameboards without degree-one vertices
statement:
Let a **gameboard** be a graph on which the Game of Cycles is played, and let its total number of edges be the number of edges in the graph. Assume that no vertex of the gameboard has degree $1$.

**Parity conjecture.** Player 1 has a winning strategy when the gameboard has an odd number of total edges, and Player 2 has a winning strategy when it has an even number of total edges.

This modifies the parity conjecture of Alvarado et al. by excluding gameboards with degree-one vertices, in response to the counterexample described in the paper. The parser marks this candidate as disproved; the displayed counterexample shows that the unrestricted parity principle fails, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether this restricted formulation itself has been disproved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.05147

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2022).
source_name: Christopher Barua, Eric Burkholder, Gabriel Fragoso and Zsuzsanna Szaniszlo, “The Game of Cycles for Grids and Select Theta Graphs”, arXiv:2208.05147 (2023).
